questions.question: You are building a machine learning model to predict the probability that a customer will click on an advertisement. You have a dataset of historical ad impressions, but the dataset contains a lot of missing values in the user features. You want to use a technique that can impute the missing values while also capturing the relationships between the user features and the ad features. Which of the following techniques would be MOST appropriate for this use case?
answers: Removing all ad impressions with missing user features.
Imputing the missing user features with the mean or median of the feature.
Imputing the missing user features with a constant value, such as 0.
Using a matrix factorization technique to impute the missing user features based on the relationships between users and ads.
feedbacks: Removing data can lead to information loss.
Mean/median imputation does not capture relationships with ad features.
Constant imputation does not capture relationships with ad features.
Matrix factorization can capture user-ad relationships for imputation.
questions.explanation: Using a matrix factorization technique to impute the missing user features based on the relationships between users and ads is an effective way to handle missing data while also capturing the relationships between the user and ad features.

questions.question: You are building a machine learning model to classify text documents. You want to use a technique that can capture the sequential order of words in the documents and their relationships. Which of the following techniques would be MOST appropriate for this use case?

questions.explanation: Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are designed to capture the sequential order of words in a text document and their relationships, making them well-suited for tasks such as sentiment analysis and text classification.
